messages.text: Searched the web · bitaxe web flasher AxeOS factory gamma 601

Hey,

Yes, you can go back to stock AxeOS. Doing it over USB with the official Bitaxe Web Flasher is the cleanest way, because it wipes Harlo OS off completely rather than trying to update over the top of it. 
The Bitaxe Web Flasher is the open source tool for flashing a factory file to your device: you connect the device, select the model and board version, and click flash.
 It is linked from https://github.com/bitaxeorg/bitaxe-web-flasher.

Before you start, open the Harlo OS settings page and write down your pool stratum URL, port and worker name. A factory flash erases the Wi-Fi and pool settings, so you will need to enter them again.

To flash it, use Chrome or Edge on a desktop or laptop, because the flasher needs the browser's Web Serial support. Connect the Gamma to the computer with a USB-C cable that carries data, not a charge-only cable, and keep its normal 5V supply plugged in. Open the flasher, pick Bitaxe Gamma and board version 601, choose the latest release and flash it. Do not unplug anything until it finishes. If the computer cannot see the miner, the cable is usually the cause. Also, 
some Bitaxe versions can't directly connect to a USB-C port, and the workaround is a USB-A adapter.


After the flash, the miner reboots and broadcasts its own setup Wi-Fi network. Join that network from your phone or laptop, enter your home Wi-Fi details, and then open AxeOS at the miner's new IP address to put your pool settings back in.

AxeOS starts at the stock frequency and voltage. If you want to tune it again, 
you need to append ?oc to the end of the settings tab URL in your browser to unlock the ASIC Frequency and ASIC Core Voltage fields.
 The same advice as before applies: watch the hardware error rate, the VR temperature and power, not the MHz figure. Anything past the stock limits is at your own risk, and damage caused by too much voltage, frequency or heat may not be covered by the warranty.

I also need to correct two things from my earlier emails:

1. **Harlo OS:** JD has stopped building Harlo OS for every miner until further notice. That means no Thor X1 build or Antminer build is on the way, and I was wrong to suggest one would appear. The team is working on an alternative. There is no date or name for it yet, and you will hear about it when it is ready.
2. **Magic M. 40T:** I said it runs 40 TH/s at 650 W. That was wrong. Its stock presets are about 30, 36 and 42 TH/s, and Magic M.'s own tests measured 30.8, 36.8 and 41.4 TH/s.

If the flasher gives you any trouble, reply here with what the screen shows and I will go through it with you.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hey,

That is a nice piece of work. I opened all three screenshots, and here is what I see.

Bitaxe7, the Gamma 601, is running your v2.15.3-solo45-tune6 build. It shows 1.83 TH/s (1.89 average over the hour, 97 percent of expected) at 29.3 W and 16.0 J/TH, with the chip at 58.5 C, the VR at 54 C, the fan at 99 percent and 4 of 4 domains hashing. Those are very good numbers for a Gamma. Bear in mind that 925 MHz at 1255 mV is well into overclock territory. A BM1370 runs comfortably at about 1.2 to 1.5 TH/s, and you are past that. The 8.8 chip errors per minute your health panel flags in yellow is the figure I would watch. If it climbs while the hashrate holds flat, the chip is telling you it is at its edge.

On the auto-tune page, I would set a real ceiling in the max voltage field instead of 0 = auto, so a tune can never walk the voltage up on its own. I would also set the watt cap ····your power supply is actually rated for, not 36 W. You might also add VR temperature as an abort condition next to chip temperature and errors. On these small boards the regulator usually gives out before the chip does.

Bitaxe5, the Supra Hex 703, has 24 of 24 domains hashing, but chip 6 is making 50.5 errors per minute against 7.2 for the other five chips combined, and its domains are still hashing at 96 to 108 percent. Your page reads it correctly: the problem is that one chip at that clock, not a domain. Backing chip 6 down a step or two will most likely clean it up for very little hashrate. If your driver can only set one clock for the whole chain, you will have to tune the chain to suit its weakest chip.

There are two small things I noticed in the UI that may be bugs:

1. **Hex chip totals:** The GH/s column for each chip does not equal the sum of its four domain tiles. Chip 3's tiles add up to 729 but the column shows 868, and chip 1's add up to 803 but the column shows 762. If the two use different averaging windows, a label would save people some confusion. If not, it is worth a look.
2. **Gamma graph:** The panel is titled "Last hour", but the axis runs from "1 min ago" to "now".

On the Thor X1, and on custom firmware in general, I have to be plain with you. Running your own firmware and settings above the stock presets is at your own risk. If a unit is damaged by voltage, frequency or heat that the firmware set, the warranty may not cover it. Before you flash the X1, take a full backup of its stock firmware and make sure you have a working recovery path, so you can always get it back to factory.

If you want people to test with you, the community in our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, is very active. JD is there as @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hey,

You're welcome, and thanks for sharing the screenshots. Good luck with the X1 build. If chip 6 on the Hex is still throwing errors after you lower its clock, or anything else looks odd, send me a screenshot here and I'll go through it with you.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Thanks for the idea. I've passed it to the team that runs the pools, and someone will get back to you in this thread. I can't say whether a Bitcoin version will happen, so I won't guess.

There is one technical difference worth knowing. The Bitcoin network has hundreds of times more hashrate than Bitcoin Cash. A Bitcoin pool the size of the BCH pool would find blocks far less often, so a 50/50 split would mean much longer waits between payouts.

Handed to the team · This is a pool server configuration change, and only the pool side can make it.

Hey,

I've looked at your screenshot. On hashpower.braiins.com, Braiins rejects us-east.harlolabs.com:8888 with "Pool extranonce2 size is incompatible", so the bid was never submitted. Your 0.00044465 BTC budget is still sitting in your Braiins account.

Here is why. On a normal stratum connection, the pool gives each connection a few bytes of extranonce2 that the miner can change as it works. A rental marketplace sits between the pool and many machines, so it needs enough of those bytes to give each of them a separate slice. Port 8888 gives fewer bytes than Braiins will accept. Rental-friendly pools usually handle this the way you suggest, with a separate rental port. One example lists a port for 
NiceHash / MRR / Braiins rentals
 and notes that its 
Extranonce2 size is 8 bytes (ample headroom for rental work distribution).


Only the pool side can change this, so I've sent your request to JD with the full details. That covers the 7 bytes or more, the separate port for rentals, your solo45.braiins worker and the Braiins error. The team is off for the weekend and picks it up Monday at 10am ET. Their answer will come to you here. I can't promise the change will be made or say when, so please don't build a rental plan around it yet.

If you want to talk it through with JD sooner, he is @nullhashrate in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hey,

You're welcome. The extranonce2 request is already with JD, so you don't need to do anything else. The team picks it up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer will come here.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hey,

Thanks for the detail, it makes the problem clear. A target of 1d00ffff is the minimum difficulty from Bitcoin's earliest days, and a random prevhash means the job isn't built on any real block. So that first job could never produce a valid share on the current BCH chain. It makes sense that Braiins OS treats it as a broken pool and restarts. Each time it reconnects it gets a placeholder job again, so it loops instead of settling. Your Bitaxes mine through that first job, which is probably why they don't hit the same problem.

Only the pool side can change this, so I've sent it to JD as a separate item from the extranonce2 request. I included the S19K Pro on Braiins OS 26.10, the placeholder job details and the fact that the same miner worked on pool.harlolabs.com:8888 last month. The team picks it up Monday at 10am ET, and the answer will come to you here. I can't promise when it will change.

If you can, reply with a few lines from the Braiins OS log covering one connect and restart, with the times. That shows JD exactly what the miner received and why it gave up.

You can also reach JD sooner in our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, where he is @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hey,

Thanks for confirming. Both pool items are now with JD. One is the extranonce2 size for Braiins hashpower rentals. The other is the placeholder first job that makes Braiins OS restart. The team picks them up Monday at 10am ET, not before, and the answers will come to you here.

If you can, send a few lines from the Braiins OS log covering one connect and restart, with the times. That shows JD exactly what the miner received.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hey,

Your settings look correct. In Braiins OS the URL should be stratum+tcp://us-east.harlolabs.com:8888, the username Solo45.S19KPro and the password x. The miner is reaching the pool, so the problem isn't your configuration.

This is the same fault you reported on Saturday. When a new worker connects, the pool's first job is a placeholder that isn't built on a real block, and Braiins OS restarts instead of mining it. Only the pool side can fix that. It is already with JD, and the team is in today, so the answer will come to you here. I can't give you a time for the fix.

Until then, if you want the S19K Pro earning, add a second pool in Braiins OS as a backup. The machine will mine there while us-east.harlolabs.com:8888 rejects it, and you can drop the backup once the fix is in.

JD can work faster with a few lines from the Braiins OS log covering one connect and restart, with the times. You can send them here, or straight to him in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, where he is @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
